mainTopic: Glazed vessels for חמץ versus יין נסך, רבי עקיבא's three questions, and the twelve-month rule for gentile wine leftovers and vessels
overview: The amud opens in the middle of מרימר's answer about glazed earthenware vessels on פסח. He forbids them because liquid seeps through them, which shows they absorb, and the תורה teaches that a כלי חרס never releases what it absorbed. The גמרא asks why he permitted the same vessels after they held gentile wine. It rejects the answer that חמץ is דאורייתא and יין נסך is only דרבנן. The real answer is that חמץ is used hot and wine is used cold. Next comes a story: רבי עקיבא could not answer three questions in גינזק, and the בית המדרש answered them, including that gentile jars are permitted after twelve months. The גמרא then turns to the משנה about gentile grape seeds and skins. Wet ones are forbidden and dry ones permitted, and שמואל defines the line as twelve months. רבי יוחנן, רב זביד and רב חביבא extend this twelve-month rule, and רב חביבא's last statement continues on the next amud.

steps.title: מרימר: The vessels sweat, so they absorb and are forbidden
steps.stepSummary: מרימר answers that glazed earthenware vessels may not be used on פסח, because he sees liquid seeping out of them, which proves they absorb.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: I see that these vessels sweat. Since they sweat, they surely absorb, and so they are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: מרימר is giving his answer about whether glazed earthenware vessels can be used on פסח. He says no, because he can see they absorb.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The glaze might seem to block absorption. But מרימר sees liquid coming through to the outside of the vessel. That shows the walls take in what is inside, so the vessel holds absorbed חמץ.

keyTerms.meaning: they sweat; liquid seeps through to the outside

phrases.english: [He said] to them: I see that they sweat,
phrases.notes: This sentence starts on the previous amud. מרימר is answering whether glazed earthenware may be used on פסח.

phrases.english: and since they sweat,
they certainly absorb, and they are forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question put to מרימר just before this section about using glazed vessels on פסח.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Glazed earthenware vessels are forbidden for פסח because they visibly sweat, which proves they absorb.

steps.title: Why purging does not help: earthenware never releases what it absorbed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the vessels cannot simply be purged, and answers that the תורה teaches a כלי חרס never fully releases what it absorbed.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason they cannot be fixed? The תורה testified about an earthenware vessel that it never lets out what is in its walls.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the vessels stay forbidden forever instead of being cleaned with hot water. It answers from the תורה's rule about earthenware.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Many vessels can be made usable by הגעלה, purging with boiling water. A כלי חרס is different: what it absorbs stays in its walls for good. Since the glazed vessels are earthenware and do absorb, they can never be made permitted for פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: the תורה testified (taught as a fact)

steps.whatToRemember: A כלי חרס that absorbed forbidden food can never be purged. Since glazed vessels visibly absorb, they are forbidden for פסח.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
phrases.notes: He means: why can't we just purge them with boiling water?

phrases.english: The Torah testified about an earthenware vessel
that it never comes out of the grip of its walls.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא? הַתּוֹרָה הֵעִידָה עַל כְּלִי חֶרֶס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the absorption described in step 1 leads to a permanent prohibition.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why can't the absorbed vessels be purged?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The תורה teaches that earthenware never releases what it absorbed.

steps.title: Challenge: מרימר permitted the same vessels for gentile wine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why חמץ is different from יין נסך, since מרימר himself taught that glazed vessels are permitted even after holding gentile wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: How is this different from יין נסך? מרימר taught them that all glazed vessels are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a contradiction in מרימר's rulings. For חמץ he forbids glazed vessels, but for gentile wine he permits them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If glazed vessels absorb, they should absorb wine too and be forbidden. Yet מרימר permitted them for יין נסך. So why do they count as absorbing for one and not the other?

keyTerms.meaning: wine of idol worship; here gentile wine

phrases.english: What is different from libation wine,
that Mareimar taught them:
all glazed earthenware vessels are permitted?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges מרימר's ruling in step 1 using his own lenient ruling about wine.
steps.kashyaTarget: מרימר's ruling that glazed vessels are forbidden for חמץ
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If glazed vessels absorb, they should be forbidden for יין נסך too, yet מרימר permitted them.

steps.title: Rejected answer: דאורייתא versus דרבנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests חמץ is stricter because it is דאורייתא while יין נסך here is דרבנן, but rejects this because the רבנן modeled their rules on תורה law.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say: חמץ is from the תורה and gentile wine is only rabbinic, that does not work. Everything the רבנן set up, they set up like the תורה's rules.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible answer to the challenge and then knocks it down right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The suggested difference is that a rabbinic prohibition might be treated more leniently. But there is a rule that rabbinic laws follow the same pattern as תורה laws. So the wine should be treated like חמץ, and this answer fails.

keyTerms.meaning: they set it up like the תורה law

steps.confusionAlert: The phrase 'וְכִי תֵּימָא' introduces an answer only so the גמרא can reject it. It is not the final answer.

phrases.english: And if you would say: leavened bread is from the Torah,
libation wine is rabbinic —
but everything that the Sages instituted,
they instituted like Torah law!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises and rejects a possible answer to the challenge in step 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that the דאורייתא/דרבנן difference explains מרימר's two rulings
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Rabbinic laws are built to match תורה laws, so a rabbinic prohibition is not treated more leniently in this way.

steps.title: Real answer: חמץ is used hot, wine is used cold
steps.stepSummary: The difference is that חמץ is used with hot food, which is absorbed deeply, while wine is kept cold and absorbed much less.
steps.simpleTranslation: This one is used with hot food, and that one is used cold.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the real answer to why מרימר ruled differently for חמץ and for wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Heat makes a vessel absorb much more. חמץ is often cooked in the vessel, so it soaks in deeply. Wine is stored and drunk cold, so the glazed vessel does not take it in the same way.
steps.whatToRemember: Glazed earthenware is forbidden for חמץ because it is used hot, but permitted after יין נסך because wine is used cold.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that how a vessel is used, hot or cold, decides how much it absorbs and how strict the rule is.

phrases.english: This one's use is with hot things,
phrases.notes: 'This one' is חמץ, which is often cooked in the vessel.

phrases.english: and that one's use is with cold things.

steps.triggerLanguage: זֶה תַּשְׁמִישׁוֹ בְּחַמִּין, וְזֶה תַּשְׁמִישׁוֹ בְּצוֹנֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 4's answer failed, gives the accepted answer to step 3's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the cases by how the vessel is used
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Glazed vessels should be treated the same for חמץ and wine.
steps.terutzMaskana: Hot use with חמץ causes deep absorption; cold use with wine does not, so the rulings differ.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא in גינזק is asked three questions he cannot answer
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא visits גינזק and is asked three questions: fasting for part of a day, gentile jars, and what משה wore during the ימי המלואים. He has no answer to any of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא came to גינזק. They asked him: Does one fast for hours or not? He did not know. Are gentile jars forbidden or permitted? He did not know. In what did משה serve all seven days of the inauguration? He did not know.
steps.whatsHappening: A new story begins. The people of גינזק ask רבי עקיבא three questions, and he cannot answer any of them. The גמרא will go through the answers next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The middle question, about gentile jars, ties to this sugya's topic of vessels that absorbed forbidden wine. The other two questions are on different subjects. The story sets up the answers that come afterward.

keyTerms.meaning: fasting for part of a day
he did not have it (he did not know)
the seven days when the משכן was set up and the כהנים were installed

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva happened to come to Ginzak,
they asked him:
Does one fast for hours,
phrases.notes: This means fasting for only part of a day and having it count as a fast.

phrases.english: or does one not fast for hours?
He did not have it.
Jars of gentiles,
are they forbidden or permitted?
He did not have it.
In what did Moses serve
all seven days of the inauguration?
phrases.notes: They are asking what clothes משה wore while serving.

phrases.english: He did not have it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story; its jar question connects to the earlier discussion of vessels that held gentile wine.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three questions were put to רבי עקיבא in גינזק and he could not answer them; the answers follow afterward.

steps.title: The study hall answers רבי עקיבא's three questions
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא brings his three questions to the בית המדרש. They rule that one may fast for part of a day, that gentile jars are permitted after twelve months, and that משה served in a white cloak.
steps.simpleTranslation: He came and asked in the study hall. They said: The הלכה is that one may fast for hours, and if he completed the day he says the fast-day prayer. The הלכה is that gentile jars are permitted after twelve months. What did משה wear when he served during the seven days of inauguration? A white cloak.
steps.whatsHappening: The three questions that רבי עקיבא could not answer in גינזק are now answered, one by one, in the בית המדרש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each of the three open questions from step 6 gets a clear ruling. For our topic the important answer is the second one: gentile wine jars become permitted once twelve months have passed. The twelve-month idea comes back again in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: The study hall, where the Sages decided questions
Fasting for hours, meaning fasting for only part of a day
The special prayer said on a fast day
The seven days of inauguration of the משכן, when משה served as כהן

steps.confusionAlert: Only the jar ruling belongs to our topic of gentile wine. The answers about fasting and about משה's clothing are given here because they were part of the same set of three questions.

phrases.english: He came and asked in the study hall,
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבי עקיבא, coming back from גינזק with the three questions he couldn't answer.

phrases.english: They said: The halacha is that one may fast for hours,
and if he completed the day, he prays the fast-day prayer.
And the halacha is that jars of gentiles
are permitted after twelve months.
In what clothing did Moshe serve
during the seven days of inauguration?
In a white cloak.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the three questions that were left open in step 6
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The answers to רבי עקיבא's three questions
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Fasting for hours is allowed. Gentile jars are permitted after twelve months. משה served in a white cloak.

steps.title: רב כהנא: the white cloak had no hem
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא teaches the answer in a more exact form: משה's white cloak had no hem.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא teaches: In a white cloak that has no hem.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא adds one detail to the third answer about משה's clothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The basic answer, a white cloak, does not change. רב כהנא's version only describes the cloak more exactly: it was made without a hem.

keyTerms.meaning: Teaches, meaning he passes the teaching on in this wording

phrases.english: Rav Kahana teaches:
In a white cloak that has no hem.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a more exact wording of the last answer in step 7
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משה's white cloak was made without a hem.

steps.title: Gentile grape seeds and skins: wet ones are forbidden, dry ones are permitted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about gentile grape seeds and skins. A ברייתא then teaches that wet ones are forbidden and dry ones are permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: The grape seeds and grape skins of gentiles, and so on. The Rabbis taught: Grape seeds and grape skins of gentiles that are wet are forbidden, and those that are dry are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic from the משנה. It brings a ברייתא that divides gentile grape leftovers into wet and dry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The leftovers of pressed grapes may still hold some of the gentile's wine. The ברייתא says that while they are wet they are forbidden, but once they are dry they are permitted. It does not yet say what counts as 'wet' or 'dry', and the next step asks exactly that.

phrases.english: The grape seeds and grape skins of gentiles, and so on.
The Rabbis taught:
Grape seeds and grape skins of gentiles:
wet ones are forbidden,
dry ones are permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַחַרְצַנִּים וְהַזַּגִּים שֶׁל גּוֹיִם וְכוּ׳. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה after the רבי עקיבא story ends
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wet gentile grape seeds and skins are forbidden, and dry ones are permitted.

steps.title: What counts as wet and what counts as dry?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a definition of the ברייתא's words 'wet' and 'dry'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which are the wet ones, and which are the dry ones?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a plain clarifying question, and this sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'wet' and 'dry' are not exact. Is it about how they feel, or about how much time has passed? The גמרא wants a clear line.

phrases.english: Which are the wet ones,
and which are the dry ones?

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵי נִינְהוּ לַחִין וְהֵי נִינְהוּ יְבֵשִׁין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the words used in the ברייתא in step 9
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How to tell apart 'wet' grape leftovers from 'dry' ones

steps.title: שמואל: wet means within twelve months, dry means after twelve months
steps.stepSummary: שמואל defines the terms by time: for the first twelve months they count as wet, and after that they count as dry.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: 'Wet' means the whole first twelve months. 'Dry' means after twelve months.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers the question by giving a set amount of time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Wet' and 'dry' do not depend on how the seeds look or feel. They depend on the calendar, and twelve months is the dividing line. This is the same twelve-month rule given for gentile jars in step 7.

keyTerms.meaning: Twelve months, the time after which the forbidden wine is considered gone

steps.whatToRemember: Gentile grape seeds and skins are forbidden for the first twelve months and permitted after that, just like gentile jars.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel:
'Wet' means the whole first twelve months,
'dry' means after twelve months.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the definition question from step 10
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Within twelve months they count as wet and are forbidden. After twelve months they count as dry and are permitted.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: forbidden even for benefit, permitted even for eating
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains how strong each status is. Before twelve months even benefit is forbidden, and after twelve months even eating is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was said: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: When they are forbidden, they are forbidden even for benefit. When they are permitted, they are permitted even to eat.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching tells us how far each status reaches, both the forbidden one and the permitted one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think the wet stage forbids only eating, or that the dry stage allows only benefit. רבי יוחנן says no: each stage goes all the way. Wet leftovers are fully forbidden, even for benefit, like יין נסך, and dry ones are fully permitted, even to eat.

keyTerms.meaning: Benefit, any use that gives a person gain

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the twelve-month line is a full switch: it takes the leftovers from completely forbidden to completely permitted.

phrases.aramaic: אִתְּמַר, אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: It was said: Rabba bar bar Chana said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
When they are forbidden, they are forbidden even for benefit,
when they are permitted, they are permitted even for eating.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִתְּמַר, אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on שמואל's time line and explains how strong each status is
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Before twelve months the leftovers are forbidden even for benefit. After twelve months they are permitted even to eat.

steps.title: רב זביד: Aramean wine dregs are permitted after twelve months
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד applies the twelve-month rule to the dregs left from the wine of Arameans.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זביד said: These dregs of the wine of the Arameans are permitted after the twelve months of a year.
steps.whatsHappening: רב זביד brings another item that follows the same twelve-month rule: wine dregs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wine dregs, like grape seeds and skins, have soaked up gentile wine. They follow the same time limit and become permitted after twelve months.

keyTerms.meaning: Dregs or yeast, the thick leftovers at the bottom of wine

phrases.english: Rav Zevid said:
These dregs of the wine of the Arameans,
after the twelve months of a year, are permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב זְבִיד: הַאי דּוּרְדְּיָּא דְּחַמְרָא דַּאֲרַמָּאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the twelve-month rule to a new item, wine dregs
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Gentile wine dregs are permitted after twelve months.

steps.title: רב חביבא בריה דרבא: jugs are permitted after twelve months
steps.stepSummary: רב חביבא בריה דרבא applies the same twelve-month rule to gentile jugs.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חביבא, the son of רבא, said: These jugs are permitted after the twelve months of a year.
steps.whatsHappening: Another אמורא adds one more item to the twelve-month list: jugs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Jugs that held gentile wine also become permitted after twelve months. This matches the בית המדרש's ruling about jars in step 7.

keyTerms.meaning: Jugs, large clay containers for wine
The twelve months of a year

phrases.english: Rav Chaviva, son of Rava, said:
These jugs,
after the twelve months of a year, are permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חֲבִיבָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא: הָנֵי גּוּלְפֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds jugs to the list of things permitted after twelve months
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Gentile wine jugs are permitted after twelve months.

steps.title: רב חביבא begins another teaching
steps.stepSummary: רב חביבא starts another statement about 'these' items, and it continues in the next part of the daf.
steps.whatsHappening: This is only the opening of a new statement. The גמרא is setting up the next teaching, which continues in the following text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far we only have the speaker and the word 'these'. Which items he means, and his ruling about them, come right after this.

phrases.english: Rav Chaviva said: These...

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a further statement in the same list of twelve-month teachings
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Not yet stated; the ruling continues in the following text.
